config.prompt: Holding a 2 kg ball 35 cm out on a forearm whose flexor inserts 5 cm from the joint axis — roughly how hard must it pull, in newtons?
config.why: F × 0.05 = (2 × 9.81) × 0.35 ≈ 6.9 N·m, so about 137 N — roughly seven times the ball's weight; the hand repays it with a seven-times larger arc at seven times the speed.

activities.caption: place the footstrike force on the scale
activities.name: bioGrfPlace

config.prompt: At footstrike, the biggest ground reaction forces in sprinting reach how many body weights? Place the value:
config.why: Roughly 3–5 times body weight — and the skill is applying large horizontal force briefly: at top speed, ground contact lasts under about 0.09 s.

activities.anchor: stiff landings are fine if you are strong enough
activities.caption: true or false — the landing bill
activities.name: bioStiffJudge

statements.s: Strength training changes the size of the landing bill.
statements.why: The momentum change is fixed by the landing; only the payment schedule — the stopping time — changes its size.

statements.s: The same momentum change stopped in 0.05 s costs about four times what it costs stopped in 0.2 s.
statements.why: About 4,400 N versus about 1,100 N for a 70 kg athlete landing at 3.1 m/s.

statements.s: Bending the hips, knees and ankles is force management, not weakness.
statements.why: Extending the stopping time is exactly what crash mats and drawing the hands back do.

statements.s: Absorbing impact quickly demonstrates strength that protects joints.
statements.why: The bill is fixed — speed of payment only changes its size; the tissues at the joint see forces many times the external load.

activities.anchor: The fuel side completes the picture
activities.caption: order the fuel systems on the timescale
activities.name: bioEnergyOrder

config.prompt: Order the supply chain of an all-out effort:
items: ATP-PC system — powers about the first 10 seconds
Anaerobic glycolysis — roughly 10 seconds to 2 minutes, accumulating fatigue metabolites
Aerobic system — everything longer, on carbohydrate and fat with the oxygen delivered
After the effort: EPOC — the respiratory system repaying the oxygen debt
config.why: Each system hands off to the next on the timescale — and exercise remodels the machinery that runs them.

activities.caption: which curve is the force–velocity relationship?
activities.name: bioFvTrace

config.prompt: Which curve is the force–velocity relationship?
config.why: Maximal force at zero speed (isometric), maximal speed under minimal load — and training shifts the whole curve upward rather than moving the athlete along it.

activities.anchor: Drag force scales with the square of speed
activities.caption: feel the cube law
activities.name: bioDragPlotter

config.why: At 10 m/s with CdA 0.3: the resistive load ≈ 18 N, power ≈ 180 W; double the velocity and power is 1,440 W — eight times for twice the pace, which is why aero positions and drafting dominate time-trialling.

activities.anchor: stronger muscles automatically mean better performance
activities.caption: true or false — what throws actually need
activities.name: bioTimingJudge

statements.why: Speed, timing and technique determine when and where the force arrives.

statements.s: Throwing velocity correlates poorly with arm strength alone and well with sequential timing.
statements.why: The kinetic chain: the arm is the last link in a chain that started at the floor.

statements.s: The fastest throwers are those who delay the arm best.
statements.why: Each segment decelerates as it transfers momentum to the next — the whip sequence.

statements.s: The biggest shoulders win the throwing contests.
statements.why: Not in the lesson's evidence — timing beats bulk.

activities.anchor: non-contact ACL ruptures have an identified signature
activities.caption: estimate the prevention dividend
activities.name: bioAclEstimate

config.prompt: Neuromuscular prevention programmes (FIFA 11+ and descendants) cut knee-ligament and other injury rates by roughly what percentage, where properly adopted?
config.why: Roughly 30–50% where properly adopted — biomechanics as measured public health.
